sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate differs from G. dilatatus in the narrower head, the larger ocelli, the differently shaped compound eyes, the wider pronotum, the narrower anterolateral angles of the pronotum and the narrower wings; from G. concavifrons, which has smaller and differently shaped compound eyes and a rounded posterior lateral margin of the pronotum; G. brevicaudatus is smaller in all dimensions and G. buttel-reepent larger in all dimensions. The soldier differs from G. dilatatus in the depressed and concave frons, the shorter mandibles, the 1st marginal tooth of the left mandible lying closer to the apex of the apical tooth, the weaker mid-constriction of the postmentum, and the wider pronotum with a slightly concave posterior lateral margin; from G. concavifrons, which has longer mandibles, the tip of the 1st marginal tooth of the left mandible farther from the apex of the apical tooth (0.48 mm), a longer posterior margin and a narrower, shorter pronotum; from G. brevicaudatus, which has a longer and wider head, shorter mandibles, a weak and blunt anterior dorsal projection of the frons, and a narrower pronotum with a rounded posterior lateral margin.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellowish brown, the frons slightly darker; labrum pale yellow; mandibles almost black at the tip, reddish brown in the middle, faintly yellowish at the base; pronotum yellow with pale brown patches; legs and tergites pale yellow. Head with a few scattered erect setae; margins and disc of the pronotum with erect setae of two lengths, long and short. Head narrow and elongate, slightly narrower behind; anterior dorsal projection distinct and pointed; frons depressed, concave. Compound eyes large, nearly oval. Anterior margin of the labrum straight. Mandibles long, the outer base raised; left mandible with 3 marginal teeth, the first nearly conical, the second with a concave posterior edge; right mandible with 2 marginal teeth, the tip of the 1st marginal tooth 0.38 mm from the apex of the apical tooth. Postmentum at its widest less than twice its narrowest width. Antennae 11—12-segmented; the 3rd segment equal to or shorter than the 2nd, the 4th equal to or longer than the 3rd. Pronotum almost as wide as the head, wider in some specimens; anterior margin concave; sides convex; posterior lateral margins slightly concave, meeting the slightly concave posterior margin. Femora slender. Measurements (mm; 6 soldiers, means in parentheses): head length (to the lateral base of the mandibles) 2.14—2.25 (2.19); head width 1.22—1.39 (1.30); head height 1.13—1.24 (1.18); left mandible length 1.01—1.09 (1.06); postmentum greatest width 0.45—0.47 (0.46), least width 0.23—0.30 (0.28), length 1.46—1.65 (1.56); pronotal median length 0.60—0.77 (0.66), maximum length 0.79—0.90 (0.83), width 1.29—1.54 (1.35); hind tibia length 0.90—0.98 (0.92).

note: Adapted from the original English description of Krishna & Emerson 1962 (new species). Type locality: a swamp forest at Kateman, on the east coast of southern Sumatra; the soldier holotype and paratype, a third-form king and queen, and nymphs were collected by H. Kirby in May 1935 (month 5), number T-4562, and the alate morphotype and paramorphotype are numbered T-4538. The original describes the alate first and the soldier second; in this scan only the last sentence of the alate section survives (wings extending beyond the scale, about 1.20—1.35 mm from the suture), and the column order of Table 10 (measurements of 9 alates) is displaced in the OCR and the values are incomplete, so the alate measurements have not been transcribed and their diagnostic characters are merged into "Diagnostic characters". The soldier measurements are translated verbatim from Table 11 of the original (holotype / range / mean), in mm; the original table heading is misprinted "MEASUREMEN'S", and spacing between punctuation and numerals in the table, such as "1.22-—1.39" and "0. 23-0. 30", has been corrected without changing the values. The name "G. buttel-reepent Holmgren" cited in the comparisons is probably an OCR misspelling and has not been changed. The worker was not described in the original.
